description: Single passkey credential with complete metadata preservation

validations.encryptMatch: byte-for-byte match of serialized container JSON
validations.decryptMatch: parsed plaintext state must match inputs.plaintextState
validations.roundTrip: decrypt -> migrate -> re-encrypt: the rewritten state MUST equal expected.roundTripState. The only permitted change is S.schemaVersion 3 to 4; there is no byte-identical requirement against the version 3 input

description: Multiple passkeys with credential-bound PRF selection

validations.prfSelection: must select by credentialId match and use entry hkdfSalt/hkdfInfo
validations.roundTrip: decrypt -> migrate -> re-encrypt: the rewritten state MUST equal expected.roundTripState. The only permitted change is S.schemaVersion 3 to 4; there is no byte-identical requirement against the version 3 input

description: An unrecognised top-level S field survives decrypt -> re-encrypt

validations.preserved: S.somethingNotYetSpecified MUST be byte-identical after decrypt -> re-encrypt
validations.rationale: A reader that strips what it does not recognise destroys a newer client's state

description: An event type the reader does not know is refused cleanly, not merged

validations.refuse: The reader MUST refuse to rewrite and report an unsupported version. It MUST NOT crash, drop the event or write a merged history
validations.rationale: An event type the reader does not know belongs to a newer version

description: Two devices writing different keys in one namespace both survive the merge

validations.bothRetained: S.extensions['org.siros.wscd'] MUST contain BOTH kid-a1b2 and kid-c3d4
validations.rationale: This is the case a per-subsystem key loses: one aggregate blob per plugin means last-write-wins discards an enrolled authenticator

description: A tombstone deletes, and is not resurrected by a peer at the fold horizon

validations.deleted: S.extensions['org.siros.bbs'] MUST NOT contain 1849302113 after the merge
validations.rationale: The tombstone is the newest write; folding it away lets an older peer's value win

description: A peer beyond the fold horizon is an unresolvable divergence, not a merge

inputs.note: Two histories with no reachable common ancestor, the ancestor having been folded into S

validations.noSilentMerge: The implementation MUST NOT concatenate the histories and present the result as merged
validations.userChoice: The divergence MUST be surfaced so the user can choose which wallet is authoritative
validations.rationale: Concatenation yields an invalid event chain; failing opaquely leaves the user with no way forward

description: Per-namespace size accounting is reported for a large container

validations.perNamespace: Sizes MUST be reportable per namespace, not only for the container as a whole
validations.rationale: Absolute size cannot be predicted; identifying the responsible namespace is what makes a limit actionable

description: Folding an lww namespace is order-independent: a partial fold and a full fold converge

validations.converges: Folding any prefix and then applying the remainder MUST yield value v3
validations.rationale: This is what lets a client fold an lww namespace it does not understand without making the outcome depend on which client folded

description: Equal timestamps are broken by eventId, deterministically

validations.deterministic: The merged value MUST be 'from-B' (greater eventId at equal timestamp), on every client
validations.rationale: Ordering on timestamp alone leaves two clients free to disagree about identical input

description: A client ignores, but preserves, extension events for a namespace it does not recognise

validations.notAnError: An unrecognised namespace MUST NOT be treated as an error
validations.retained: The event MUST remain in events after a merge, and its state MUST NOT be discarded
validations.rationale: A client must be able to carry state for a data kind it has not yet learned

description: Two versions of one namespace coexist; neither client deletes the other's state

validations.bothRetained: A client supporting only org.siros.bbs/v2 MUST leave org.siros.bbs entries intact
validations.noMigration: The client MUST NOT be required to produce v2 state for cred-old
validations.drain: cred-old's entry is removed only when the credential it names is deleted
validations.rationale: v2 holder state cannot be synthesised for a credential issued under v1 - the issuance handshake cannot be replayed - so coexistence is the steady state, not a transition

description: Credential metadata (string, number, object, nested array, unicode, duplicate type) plus an unknown per-credential member and an unknown top-level S member all survive decrypt -> re-encrypt

validations.roundTrip: decrypt -> re-encrypt MUST yield state identical to expected.roundTripState
validations.metadataOrder: S.credentials[0].metadata entries MUST keep their order, including both entries of type example.dup
validations.metadataOpaque: values MUST be preserved as JSON values, including null nested inside an object and the empty array nested inside an array
validations.unknownMembers: S.credentials[0].x-unknown-credential-member and S.x-unknown-top-level MUST be preserved with identical values; an implementation that cannot MUST refuse to rewrite

description: metadata absent: reader accepts, writer does not add it

validations.roundTrip: re-encrypted state MUST NOT contain a metadata member on the credential
validations.writer: a writer MUST NOT emit metadata: null

description: metadata: [] is accepted by a reader; a writer MUST NOT emit it

validations.reader: decrypting plaintextState MUST succeed and be treated as no metadata
validations.writer: state written back MUST equal expected.roundTripState, i.e. without a metadata member (neither null nor [])

description: Unknown members of S.credentials[] entries survive decrypt -> re-encrypt

validations.roundTrip: every unknown member of every credential entry MUST be preserved with an identical value; a reader that cannot preserve it MUST refuse to rewrite
validations.rationale: Preservation is not limited to the six named wallet metadata fields

description: An unknown top-level S member survives decrypt -> re-encrypt (credential-entry-level companion of extensions-unknown-field-001)

validations.roundTrip: S.x-unknown-top-level MUST be preserved with an identical value

description: A container whose S.schemaVersion the reader does not implement is refused, not rewritten

validations.refuse: A version 4 reader MUST refuse to rewrite the container and report an unsupported version, not a failed merge. It MUST NOT lower schemaVersion or write the container back
validations.rationale: Version 5 may define members or events that a version 4 reader would drop

description: An event whose schemaVersion the reader does not implement is refused, even when S.schemaVersion and the event type are known

validations.refuse: A version 4 reader MUST refuse to rewrite the container and report an unsupported version. It MUST NOT apply, drop or rewrite the event
validations.rationale: The version check applies to every event, not only to S

description: An event type that no implemented version defines is refused in a single container (companion of extensions-unknown-event-001, which covers a merge)

validations.refuse: A version 4 reader MUST refuse to rewrite the container and report an unsupported version. It MUST NOT crash, drop the event or skip it during reduction
validations.rationale: A new event type needs a new version, so an unknown type means the container is newer than the reader

description: An event without an integer schemaVersion is refused, even when its type is known

validations.refuse: A version 4 reader that rewrites MUST refuse and report an unsupported version. It MUST NOT assume a version, apply, drop or rewrite the event
validations.rationale: Every event carries an integer schemaVersion; an unversioned event cannot be attributed to an implemented version

description: Migrating a version 3 container to version 4 only sets S.schemaVersion to 4

validations.migration: The written state MUST equal expected.roundTripState: S.schemaVersion is 4 and nothing else changes
validations.events: Existing events keep schemaVersion 3 as authored; only new events carry 4

description: A version 3 container written before Spec 3.0 that already carries metadata and S.extensions is read as version 4

validations.reader: A version 4 reader MUST accept the container and read metadata and S.extensions as version 4 members
validations.migration: The written state MUST equal expected.roundTripState: S.schemaVersion is 4, metadata and S.extensions are preserved with identical values

description: Storing credential metadata or an extension into a version 3 container writes a version 4 container

validations.writer: The written S.schemaVersion MUST be 4 and the set_extension event MUST carry schemaVersion 4
validations.forbidden: A written container with S.schemaVersion 3 MUST NOT carry metadata on any credential entry, S.extensions, or a set_extension event

description: Every event type a version 4 reader implements (the nine of wallet-frontend plus set_extension) with its real shape and schemaVersion 4 is accepted and round-trips unchanged

validations.roundTrip: The written state MUST equal expected.roundTripState; events are preserved as authored
validations.eventTypes: The ten event types of Section 6 each occur at least once
validations.baseState: S is the base snapshot before the pending events; the events create every entity, so folding them over S duplicates nothing
validations.eventChain: lastEventHash is empty; events[0].parentHash equals it and every later parentHash is the hash of the previous event (SHA-256 hex of the event with sorted keys, compact JSON; for new_keypair with keypair.wrappedPrivateKey set to null), as wallet-frontend's validateEventHistoryContinuity requires

description: Keypair entries that a reader cannot parse or does not know (an unknown member, a legacy shape, a non-object) are preserved verbatim on rewrite

validations.roundTrip: decrypt -> re-encrypt MUST yield state identical to expected.roundTripState; an implementation that cannot preserve an S.keypairs[] entry or member MUST refuse to rewrite the container rather than drop it

description: nym_auth delivered secret: SHA256(secret_seed) must equal the issuer-signed ssc; the entries are stored as an auxiliary_data metadata entry

cases.name: match
cases.expected: accept: store secret_seed in credential metadata

cases.name: mismatch
cases.expected: failed issuance: do not store, do not use

validations.commitment: SHA256(bytes.fromhex(secret_seed_hex)) MUST equal ssc_hex before storing and again before use
validations.mismatch: a mismatch MUST be treated as a failed issuance

description: Response-level credential_metadata (OpenID4VCI#721 shape) with auxiliary_data: single entry, batch, two entries, unknown member preserved

cases.name: batch of three credentials share one seed
two entries, the hash_commitment one verified
unknown member ignored and preserved in order

expected.rule: each response-level credential_metadata member becomes one metadata entry {type: member name, value: member value verbatim} in every credential of the response

description: Plain response (immediate or deferred), missing notification_id, commitment mismatch, no entry for the committed claim and credential_metadata as an array are refused

cases.name: no hash_commitment entry for the committed claim
credential_metadata is an array, not an object
plain (unencrypted) deferred credential response carrying a seed

expected.rule: failed issuance; seed not stored or used

description: Strip auxiliary_data from the response credential_metadata before merging into display metadata; the entries go only to the secret store

cases.name: seed only in response, nothing in issuer metadata
unknown member survives the merge, auxiliary_data does not

expected.rule: merge is a member-wise overwrite of issuer metadata by the stripped response object; the seed hex appears nowhere in the merged display metadata
